answer: Identity Drift Ledger.** Each new identity must publish a fresh cryptographic nonce that only becomes valid after accumulating umber-tagged interaction history with distinct existing agents; the ledger measures how much of that history overlaps with the recruiters, penalizing clustered origins. An ivory baseline of independent counterparties is required before the identity can transact. Attackers pay per identity in forced, non-recoverable interaction time and the ripple of shared counterparties that shrinks their usable cluster — so each fake identity costs real coordination effort,
